2026-12-05.title: Saturday of the First Week of Advent
readings: He will be gracious to you when you cry
Blessed are all who wait for the Lord
He had compassion for them; the harvest is plentiful
2026-12-05.alt: Optional: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2026-12-05.verse: When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
theo: Isaiah speaks tenderly to a people in distress: God “waits to be gracious to you”; “he will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry”; your Teacher will no longer hide, and “your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, ‘This is the way; walk in it.’” He promises rain, harvest, and the day when the Lord “binds up the injuries of his people”.

Jesus goes through all the towns teaching, proclaiming and healing. Seeing the crowds “harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd”, he is moved with compassion. His response is twofold: pray (“ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers”) and send (he calls the Twelve and gives them authority). “You received without payment; give without payment.” Advent compassion becomes mission.
outline: Ask: when did someone show you the way when you were lost?
Point 1 · God waits to be gracious
He hears our cry and shows the way.
Pray for labourers, and become one.
“This is the way; walk in it.”
live: Pray daily this Advent for priests, religious and lay missionaries.
Offer a free service to someone this week: tuition, a ride, a visit.
2026-12-05.prayer: Lord of the harvest, you wait to be gracious to us. Show me the way and let me walk in it. Send labourers into your harvest, and make me generous, giving freely what I have freely received. Amen.
altar: At Mass we receive freely the greatest gift of all. Sent out at the end, we are asked to give freely to others.

quick: God waits to be gracious and hears our cry.
Jesus has compassion on the harassed and helpless.
What we received freely, we give freely.
2026-12-05.action: Pray daily for vocations this Advent.
2026-12-05.question: What have I received freely that I could give freely?

family.explain: Jesus felt sorry for people who were lost, like sheep without a shepherd. He asks us to pray for helpers and to help others too.
family.intention: We pray for priests, sisters and catechists.
family.ask: Ask: “What have we received from God that we can share with others?”

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, you look with compassion on the crowds. As we gather, let us hear your voice saying: this is the way; walk in it. Amen.
share: Isaiah promises a word behind us: this is the way (Isaiah 30:21). Where do I need God's guidance now?
Jesus saw the crowds as sheep without a shepherd (Matthew 9:36). Whom do I see like that?
What have I received freely that I can give freely?
pm.resp: Lord, send labourers into your harvest.
interc: For vocations to the priesthood and religious life.
For catechists and Sunday school teachers.
For people who are harassed and helpless, that they may find a shepherd.
For those in adversity, that God may be gracious to them at the sound of their cry.
For our group, that we may be generous labourers in the harvest.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, good Shepherd, you sent your apostles to heal and proclaim. Send us too, and make us generous with what we have freely received. Amen.

illus: A retired schoolteacher in Kottayam began tutoring children from a nearby colony every evening without charge. When asked why, she said: “I received my education almost free from the sisters. I am just giving back what I received.”

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah speaks tenderly to a suffering people: he will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; when he hears it, he will answer you. Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your Teacher will not hide himself any more (Isaiah 30:19–20).

And then a beautiful promise: your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, this is the way; walk in it (Isaiah 30:21). God guides us, not always by showing the whole road, but by a quiet word at each turning.

In the Gospel Jesus goes about all the cities and villages, teaching, proclaiming the good news and curing every sickness. When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd. He tells his disciples: the harvest is plentiful, but the labourers are few (Matthew 9:35–38).

Then he does something surprising: he calls the Twelve and sends them out to do what he has been doing. Proclaim the good news, cure the sick, cleanse lepers. You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8).

Advent is not only waiting for Christ; it is also being sent by him. The crowds of our time are harassed and helpless too: young people without direction, families under stress, people lost in addictions. Jesus looks at them with compassion, and he sends us.

Let us pray today for labourers in the harvest: priests, religious, catechists and committed lay people. Let us listen for that quiet word behind us: this is the way. And let us give freely what we have freely received. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus feels sorry for people who are lost and sad. Pray today that God will send many good priests and sisters!

intro: Theme: “This is the way; walk in it.”
God waits to be gracious; Jesus has compassion; the Twelve are sent.

sub: He hears the cry of his people.
q: Therefore the LORD waits to be gracious to you; therefore he will rise up to show mercy to you. For the LORD is a God of justice; blessed are all those who wait for him.
When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
points.apply: Bring your deepest cry to God today.

sub: Advent is about finding the way.
q: And when you turn to the right or when you turn to the left, your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it.”
The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’
points.apply: Ask God for guidance in one decision.

q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
Cure the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
points.apply: Offer a free service to someone this week.

concl: Walk in his way, and share what you have received.
2026-12-05.resolve: Pray each day of Advent for vocations from your parish.
